name: Post-Earnings Announcement Drift Feasibility Check (Ball & Brown 1968; Bernard & Thomas 1989)
source: Ball & Brown (1968) "An Empirical Evaluation of Accounting Income Numbers"; Bernard & Thomas (1989) "Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?", Journal of Accounting Research 27: 1-36.
hypothesis: Stocks drift in the direction of earnings surprises for weeks/months after announcement. Standardized Unexpected Earnings (SUE) = (Actual EPS - Expected EPS) / StdDev(Actual EPS - Expected EPS). Long top quintile SUE, short bottom quintile SUE (dollar-neutral), hold 60 trading days post-announcement.

yfinance_availability.earnings_dates: ~25 quarters per ticker, earliest ~2020-10 to 2021-02 across all tickers

data_feasibility_check.rationale: yfinance earnings dates only available from ~2020. A 504-day formation window requires data from ~2012-2013. The earliest possible walk-forward would start in ~2022, making a 2014-2026 backtest impossible. Only ~6 years of earnings history vs required 12+ years.

decision: DATA-INFEASIBLE - cannot support pre-registered 2014-2026 walk-forward with 504-day formation window. No OOS Sharpe gate evaluated.
